saves.appliesWhen: When you attack a creature that has fewer than 100 Hit Points with this weapon and roll a 20 on the d20 for the attack roll
saves.unless: Constructs and Undead succeed on the save automatically

notes: On a failed save the creature is slain instantly. Constructs and Undead succeed on the save automatically.
The weapon loses 1 charge only if the creature is slain, and loses the property with no charges left. No regaining is stated, and the charges object cannot hold either fact, so charges is untyped.

damage.appliesWhen: When you make a ranged attack roll with this weapon against your sworn enemy

notes: Uttering the command word on a ranged attack makes the target your sworn enemy until it dies or until dawn 7 days later. Only one sworn enemy at a time.
Ranged attack rolls against your sworn enemy have Advantage, ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover, and suffer no Disadvantage from long range.
While your sworn enemy lives, you have Disadvantage on attack rolls with all other weapons.
One vial covers one Medium or smaller creature with its equipment. One more vial is needed for each size category above Medium.
Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The effect lasts 1 hour.
One vial coats one Melee weapon or twenty pieces of ammunition that are nonmagical and deal Slashing or Piercing damage.

After 1 minute of application, the coated weapon becomes a +3 Weapon or the ammunition becomes +3 Ammunition. That bonus belongs to the coated item and is not printed as a “+N bonus to”, so bonuses is untyped.
Applied to a creature (10 minutes), it gives the effect of Freedom of Movement for 8 hours. One vial covers one Medium or smaller creature, one more vial per size category above Medium.

Alternatively, poured on the ground as a Magic action, it covers a 10-foot square and duplicates the effect of Grease in that area for 8 hours. Grease carries alternativeTo 0, so the two never both apply.
As a Magic action while the pearl is on your person, you regain one expended spell slot of level 3 or lower. Once used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.
As a Magic action you regain 2d4 + 2 Hit Points. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.
You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition while you wear it.
The limited property has no printed name, so the use’s label is the few official words that name it.
While you wear it, you have Immunity to the Poisoned condition and Poison damage.
Life Preservation: on a Death Saving Throw you can change a roll of 9 or lower to a 10.
Natural Healing Boost: whenever you roll a Hit Point Die to regain Hit Points, double the Hit Points it restores.
Natural Healing Boost doubles Hit Points restored by a Hit Point Die, so healing is untyped.
The next time you see a creature within 10 minutes after drinking, you have the Charmed condition (charmed by that creature) for 1 hour. No save is stated.
Playing them is a Magic action that expends 1 charge. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet makes the save or has the Frightened condition for 1 minute.
A creature that fails repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Item saves have no timing, so saves is untyped.
A creature that succeeds on its save is immune to these pipes for 24 hours.

saves.appliesWhen: Whenever a Swarm of Rats that isn’t under another creature’s control comes within 30 feet of you while you are playing the pipes

notes: While the pipes are on your person, ordinary rats and giant rats are Indifferent toward you and won't attack unless threatened or harmed.

After playing as a Magic action, you can take a Bonus Action to expend 1 to 3 charges, calling one Swarm of Rats per charge if enough rats are within half a mile. Otherwise the charge is wasted. Calling swarms costs charges and is neither a roll, a save nor a spell, so charges is untyped.

The save is made by a Swarm of Rats not under another creature's control that comes within 30 feet while you play. On a failure it becomes Friendly and obeys you while you keep playing each round as a Magic action. On a success, or when it starts its turn more than 30 feet away, it can't be swayed for 24 hours.
Gaining the effect takes a Magic action and a command word. It ends if you remove the armor or take a Magic action to repeat the command word.
This property can't be used again until the next dawn.
Opens an extradimensional hole 10 feet deep from a 6-foot-diameter cloth. Opening and closing each take a Magic action.
A creature inside a folded hole can take an action to make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check to force its way out.
A closed hole holds air for 1 hour of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.
Placing it inside a Bag of Holding, Handy Haversack or similar space destroys both and opens a one-way gate to the Astral Plane that pulls in creatures within 10 feet not behind Total Cover.
No Concentration required.
For 1 hour you gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed and have Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to climb.
Only the "reduce" effect of Enlarge/Reduce, for 1d4 hours, no Concentration required.
For 1 hour you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover. If you're in the air when it wears off, you fall unless you have another means of staying aloft.
Lasts 1 hour, no Concentration required, or until you end it as a Bonus Action.
Your Strength score changes to the variant's score for 1 hour.
The potion has no effect if your Strength is equal to or greater than that score.
Only the "enlarge" effect of Enlarge/Reduce, for 10 minutes, no Concentration required.
You gain 10 Temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour.
The Bless effect lasts the same 1 hour, no Concentration required.
You have the Invisible condition for 1 hour. It ends early if you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell.
For 1 minute you have Resistance to all damage.
Your physical age is reduced by 1d6 + 6 years, to a minimum of 13 years.
Each later Potion of Longevity you drink has a 10 percent cumulative chance that you instead age by 1d6 + 6 years.
Lasts 10 minutes, no Concentration required.
The drinker takes the 4d6 Poison damage with no save. The save decides only the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.
It looks, smells and tastes like a Potion of Healing or another beneficial potion. Identify reveals its true nature.
You have Resistance to one damage type for 1 hour. The GM chooses the type or rolls 1d10 on the table: Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Thunder.
Lasts 1 minute, no Concentration required, and without the wave of lethargy when the effect ends.
Removes any Exhaustion levels and ends the Poisoned condition.
For 24 hours you regain the maximum number of Hit Points for any Hit Point Die you spend.
You can breathe underwater for 24 hours.

conditionalBonuses.appliesWhen: Quarterstaff Form Only). When you are hit by an attack while holding the weapon

notes: As a Bonus Action it emits or extinguishes green Dim Light out to 10 feet. It can also be lit after you roll Initiative.
As a Bonus Action it becomes a 6-inch rod, a 10-foot pole, or a Quarterstaff again.
Acrobatic Assist (Quarterstaff and 10-Foot Pole Forms Only): Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
Attack Deflection takes a Reaction, and the +5 applies against the triggering attack only. The span holds both the form and the trigger. The uses entry is Attack Deflection's.
Ranged Weapon (Quarterstaff Form Only): the Thrown property with range 30/120 feet. It flies back to your hand after a ranged attack.
As a Magic action you summon a particular Djinni within 120 feet. It stays while you maintain Concentration, up to 1 hour, or until it drops to 0 Hit Points.
The djinni is Friendly and obeys your commands. Without commands it defends itself and takes no other actions.
After it departs it can't be summoned again for 24 hours. The ring becomes nonmagical if the djinni dies.
The ring is linked to one Elemental Plane, chosen or rolled by the GM. Only the spells of that plane's row can be cast.
Elemental Bane: Advantage on attack rolls against Elementals, and they have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

Elemental Compulsion: the save is made by an Elemental you see within 60 feet when you take a Magic action. On a failure it has the Charmed condition until the start of your next turn and you decide its move and action on its next turn.

Elemental Focus: Air gives Auran, Resistance to Lightning damage, and a Fly Speed equal to your Speed with hover. Earth gives Terran, Resistance to Acid damage, ignoring rubble, rock or dirt Difficult Terrain, and moving through solid earth or rock. Fire gives Ignan and Immunity to Fire damage. Water gives Aquan, a Swim Speed of 60 feet, and water breathing.
When you fail a Dexterity saving throw while wearing the ring, you can take a Reaction to expend 1 charge and succeed on that save instead.
The charge buys a success on your own failed save, which no field holds, so charges is untyped.
When you fall, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from falling.
Difficult Terrain doesn't cost you extra movement.
Magic can neither reduce any of your Speeds nor cause you to have the Paralyzed or Restrained condition.
As a Magic action you give yourself the Invisible condition until the ring is removed or you take a Bonus Action to become visible again.
You are immune to magic that lets others read your thoughts, determine whether you are lying, know your alignment, or know your creature type. Telepathic communication with you needs your permission.
As a Magic action the ring becomes imperceptible until you take another Magic action, remove it, or die.
If you die wearing it, your soul enters the ring unless it already houses one, and can communicate telepathically with any wearer.
You regain 1d6 Hit Points every 10 minutes if you have at least 1 Hit Point.
A lost body part regrows after 1d6 + 1 days if you have at least 1 Hit Point the whole time.

You have Resistance to one damage type, shown by the gemstone and chosen or rolled on a 1d10 table: Acid (Pearl), Cold (Tourmaline), Fire (Garnet), Force (Sapphire), Lightning (Citrine), Necrotic (Jet), Poison (Amethyst), Psychic (Jade), Radiant (Topaz), Thunder (Spinel).

damage.label: Shooting Stars
damage.appliesWhen: Each creature in a 15-foot Cube originating from that point

notes: Dancing Lights and Light are cast with no charge cost stated.

Lightning Spheres: expend 2 charges as a Magic action for up to four spheres. A sphere discharges at the first creature other than you that it comes within 5 feet of. The Lightning damage by number of spheres is printed only in the table rows, half on a success, so it is not typed on the item.
Shooting Stars: expend 1 to 3 charges as a Magic action, one mote per charge. Each creature in a mote's 15-foot Cube makes the save, taking 5d4 Radiant damage on a failure or half on a success.
Each mote costs 1 charge and brings about the Shooting Stars save and its 5d4, so both carry charges 1 and the label Shooting Stars, and the cost is paid once per mote.
Stores up to 5 levels of spells. When found it holds 1d6 − 1 levels chosen by the GM.
Any creature can cast a spell of level 1 through 5 into it by touching it. The slot level sets the space used.
While wearing it you can cast any stored spell, using the original caster's slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus and spellcasting ability. No specific spell is named.
The spells cast from the ring are whatever was stored, so the typed spell list cannot hold them.
Advantage on saving throws against spells. On a successful save against a spell of level 7 or lower, the spell has no effect on you.
If that spell targeted only you and created no area of effect, you can take a Reaction to deflect it back at its caster, who saves against its own spell save DC.
The deflected spell's caster saves with its own spell save DC, which is not a printed number.
You have a Swim Speed of 40 feet.

As a Magic action you expend 1 to 3 charges for a ranged spell attack against a creature within 60 feet. The ring makes the attack roll with a +7 bonus. On a hit, for each charge spent the target takes 2d10 Force damage and is pushed 5 feet away.
Alternatively the ring tries to break a nonmagical object within 60 feet, making a Strength check with a +5 bonus per charge. That is the ring's own check, not a bonus to the user.
Breaking an object costs 1 to 3 charges and is a check, not a roll, save or spell, so charges is untyped.
No regaining of charges is stated. The ring becomes nonmagical when you use the last charge, which the charges object cannot hold.
If you take Cold damage while wearing it, the damage is reduced by 2d8.
You and what you wear and carry are unharmed by temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower.

saves.appliesWhen: Whenever you use the ring again before taking a Long Rest

notes: As a Magic action you gain X-ray vision with a range of 30 feet for 1 minute, through up to 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or 3 feet of wood or dirt. A thin sheet of lead blocks it.
The save is made only when you use the ring again before taking a Long Rest. On a failure you gain 1 Exhaustion level.
All-Around Vision: Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
Special Senses: Darkvision and Truesight, both with a range of 120 feet.

Drawbacks: a Light spell cast on the robe or a Daylight spell cast within 5 feet of it gives you the Blinded condition for 1 minute. The save is made at the end of each of your turns, ending the condition on a success. Item saves have no timing, so saves is untyped. These spells are cast by others, not by the robe.
As a Magic action expending 1 charge, the robe shows dazzling hues until the end of your next turn, shedding Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for 30 more feet.
During that time creatures that can see you have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you.
Each creature in the Bright Light that can see you when the power is activated makes the save or has the Stunned condition until the effect ends.

Casting Magic Missile takes a Magic action and expends one of six large stars. Daily at dusk, 1d6 removed stars reappear. No field holds the star cost or the dusk return, so spells and uses are untyped.
As a Magic action you enter the Astral Plane with what you wear and carry, and return with another Magic action.
Armor: if you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 15 plus your Dexterity modifier.
Magic Resistance: Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
As a Magic action you detach a patch, which becomes the object or creature it represents. The robe becomes ordinary once the last patch is removed.
It has two each of Bullseye Lantern (filled and lit), Dagger, Mirror, Pole, Rope (coiled) and Sack, plus 4d4 other patches chosen or rolled on a 1d100 table.
The table's Spell Scroll patch (one spell of level 1, 2 or 3) belongs to that row. No spell is cast by the robe.
As a Reaction you absorb a spell that targets only you and creates no area of effect. The spell is canceled and its level of energy is stored.
The rod absorbs up to 50 levels over its existence, then can't absorb more.
A spellcaster holding it can turn stored energy into spell slots to cast prepared or known spells, no higher than their own slots and at most level 5.
A newly found rod typically holds 1d10 levels. A rod that can't absorb and has no energy left becomes nonmagical.

conditionalBonuses.appliesWhen: While in that Bright Light, you and your allies
While in that Bright Light, you and your allies

notes: Alertness: while holding the rod, Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and Initiative rolls.

Protective Aura: after you plant the rod as a Magic action, it sheds Bright Light in a 60-foot radius and Dim Light for 60 more feet. You and your allies in the Bright Light gain the bonuses and sense the location of any Invisible creature also in it. It lasts 10 minutes or until the rod is pulled from the ground, and can't be used again until the next dawn.

conditionalBonuses.appliesWhen: it functions as a magic Mace
it functions as a magic Mace
transforming the rod into a magic Battleaxe
transforming the rod into a magic Battleaxe
transforming the rod into a magic Spear
transforming the rod into a magic Spear
The rod transforms into a handheld battering ram and grants its user a +10 bonus to Strength (Athletics) checks made to break through doors, barricades, and other barriers

damage.appliesWhen: the blade functions as a magic Longsword or Shortsword (your choice)

notes: Buttons are pressed as a Bonus Action. An effect lasts until another button is pushed or the same button is pushed again.
The +10 bonus needs both Button 5's form and a check made to break through a barrier, so its span is the whole sentence.
Button 1 states no attack or damage bonus for the blade. Button 4: a climbing pole. Button 6: points to magnetic north.
Drain Life: on a melee hit, the DC 17 Constitution save, and the 4d6 Necrotic on a failure. You regain Hit Points equal to half that damage.
Paralyze: on a failed save the target has the Paralyzed condition for 1 minute and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns.
Terrify: each creature you can see within 30 feet saves or has the Frightened condition for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.
The repeated saves have no timing field, so saves is untyped.

outcomes.effect: the rod disappears in a harmless burst of radiance

notes: As a Magic action, each creature of your choice you can see within 120 feet makes the save or has the Charmed condition for 8 hours, regarding you as its trusted leader.
The Charmed condition ends for a target that is harmed by you or your allies or commanded against its nature.
Once used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.
As a Magic action you and up to 199 willing creatures you can see go to a demiplane of your chosen form that sustains its visitors.
Each hour there a visitor regains Hit Points as if it had spent 1 Hit Point Die. Creatures don't age there.
Visitors can stay up to 200 days divided by the number of creatures present (round down). Once used, it can't be used again until 10 days have passed.
A 60-foot rope that holds up to 3,000 pounds. As a Magic action its far end animates and moves 10 feet per turn toward a destination, and it can fasten, unfasten, knot, unknot or coil itself.
Knotted, it shortens to 50 feet and grants Advantage on ability checks made to climb using it.
It has AC 20, HP 20, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and regains 1 Hit Point every 5 minutes while it has at least 1.
As a Magic action the rope entangles one creature you can see within 20 feet, which makes the save or has the Restrained condition.
A Restrained target can take an action to make its choice of a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, escaping on a success.
It has AC 20, HP 20, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and regains 1 Hit Point every 5 minutes while it has at least 1.
The two escape checks are the target's choice of one, not both.

Preservation: if you fail a saving throw against a Necromancy spell or a harmful effect from an Undead, you can take a Reaction to expend 1 charge and succeed instead. No regaining of charges is stated.
The scarab is destroyed when its last charge is expended, which the charges object cannot hold.
Spell Resistance: Advantage on saving throws against spells.
You can make one attack with it as a Bonus Action on each of your turns.
The target is the bearer of the other stone. If no creature bears it, you learn that and don't cast the spell.
Once Sending is cast using either stone, the stones can't be used again until the next dawn. If one stone is destroyed, the other becomes nonmagical.
While holding it, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks.
The bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC.
While holding it, you have Resistance to damage from attacks made with Ranged weapons.

Curse: attuning curses you until you are targeted by Remove Curse or similar magic. Removing the Shield doesn't end the curse. Whenever an attack with a Ranged weapon targets a creature within 10 feet of you, you become the target instead. Remove Curse is only mentioned.
The AC bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC.

Forceful Bash: when you take the Attack action, one attack roll can be made with the Shield against a target within 5 feet, adding your Proficiency Bonus and Strength modifier. On a hit, 2d6 + 2 plus your Strength modifier Force damage. You can push a creature up to 10 feet away, and give one your size or smaller the Prone condition.
Protective Field: a Reaction, an immobile 5-foot Emanation. The uses entry is this property's.
You can move on vertical surfaces and ceilings with your hands free, and have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed. Not on slippery surfaces such as ice or oil.
A container holds 1d6 + 1 ounces when found. One ounce covers a 1-foot square and takes a Utilize action to apply. It sets in 1 minute.
The bond can be broken only by Universal Solvent, Oil of Etherealness, or a Wish spell. Wish is only mentioned.

The scroll holds a single unnamed spell. If it is on your spell list you can cast it without Material components, with its normal casting time. The scroll crumbles once the spell is cast, but isn't lost if the casting is interrupted.
If the spell is of a higher level than you can normally cast, you make an ability check with your spellcasting ability, DC 10 plus the spell's level. On a failure the spell disappears.
A Wizard spell can be copied into a spellbook with an Intelligence (Arcana) check, DC 10 plus the spell's level. The scroll is destroyed either way.
The spell is whichever one the scroll bears, so no spell is typed.
While holding it, you have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, and spell attack rolls have Disadvantage against you.

damage.appliesWhen: Anything else that touches the sphere but isn’t wholly engulfed and obliterated by it

notes: The first roll is dealt to anything that touches the sphere. The second is dealt to a creature whose space the controlled sphere enters and that fails the DC 19 Dexterity save. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by it is obliterated.
Control takes a Magic action within 60 feet and the DC 25 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a failure the sphere moves 10 feet toward you.
Contact with a planar portal or extradimensional space is resolved on a 1d100 table. Gate is only mentioned.

outcomes.effect: the staff crumbles to dust and is destroyed

notes: Spells are cast using your spell save DC.

Reflect Enchantment: if you succeed on a save against an Enchantment spell that targets only you, you can take a Reaction and expend 1 charge to turn the spell back on its caster as if you had cast it. The 1 charge it costs has no field, and the spell turned back is not named, so charges and spells are untyped.
Resist Enchantment: if you fail a save against an Enchantment spell that targets only you, you can succeed instead. Once per dawn.

outcomes.effect: the staff crumbles into cinders and is destroyed

notes: You have Resistance to Fire damage while you hold the staff.
Spells are cast using your spell save DC.

outcomes.effect: the staff turns to water and is destroyed

notes: You have Resistance to Cold damage while you hold the staff.
Spells are cast using your spell save DC.

outcomes.effect: the staff vanishes in a flash of light, lost forever

notes: Cure Wounds costs 1 charge per spell level, maximum 4 for a level 4 spell.
Spells are cast using your spellcasting ability modifier.

outcomes.effect: the staff retains its +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls but loses all other properties
the staff regains 1d8 + 2 charges

notes: The attack and damage bonuses apply when it is wielded as a magic Quarterstaff. The AC, saving throw and spell attack bonuses apply while holding it.
Spells are cast using your spell save DC.

Retributive Strike: as a Magic action you break the staff, which explodes in a 30-foot Emanation. You have a 50 percent chance to travel to a random plane and avoid it. Otherwise you take Force damage equal to 16 times the charges in the staff.

Each other creature in the area makes the save, taking Force damage equal to 4 times the charges in the staff on a failure or half on a success. These amounts depend on the charges, so they are not typed as damage.

outcomes.effect: the staff becomes a nonmagical Quarterstaff

notes: When you hit with a melee attack using it, you can expend up to 3 charges. The target takes the extra 1d6 Force damage for each charge expended.

outcomes.effect: a swarm of insects consumes and destroys the staff, then disperses

notes: Spells are cast using your spell save DC and spell attack modifier.

Insect Cloud: as a Magic action expending 1 charge, harmless insects fill a 30-foot Emanation for 10 minutes, Heavily Obscured for creatures other than you. A strong wind such as Gust of Wind disperses it. Gust of Wind is only mentioned.
Insect Cloud costs 1 charge and is not a roll, save or spell, so charges is untyped.

outcomes.effect: the staff regains 1d12 + 1 charges

notes: The attack and damage bonuses apply when it is wielded as a magic Quarterstaff. The spell attack bonus applies while you hold it.
Spells are cast using your spell save DC.

Spell Absorption: Advantage on saving throws against spells. As a Reaction when another creature casts a spell that targets only you, the staff cancels it and gains charges equal to its level. If that takes it above 50 charges, it explodes as if by Retributive Strike.

Retributive Strike: as a Magic action you break the staff, which explodes in a 30-foot Emanation. You have a 50 percent chance to travel to a random plane and avoid it. Otherwise you take Force damage equal to 16 times the charges in the staff.

Each other creature in the area makes the save, taking Force damage equal to 6 times the charges in the staff on a failure or half on a success. These amounts depend on the charges, so they are not typed as damage.
Spell Absorption adds charges and can explode the staff above 50, which the charges object cannot hold.
As a Magic action you throw the staff to within 10 feet, where it becomes a Giant Constrictor Snake under your control that acts right after you on your Initiative count.
You command it mentally (no action) within 60 feet if you aren't Incapacitated.

As a Bonus Action it reverts to staff form, and the property can't be used again for 1 hour. If the snake drops to 0 Hit Points, it dies and the staff is destroyed. If it reverts first, it regains all its Hit Points.

outcomes.effect: the staff loses its properties and becomes a nonmagical Quarterstaff

notes: The attack and damage bonuses apply when it is wielded as a magic Quarterstaff. The spell attack bonus applies while holding it.
Spells are cast using your spell save DC.

Tree Form: as a Magic action expending 1 charge, the planted staff becomes a 60-foot tree. A Magic action while touching it returns it to staff form. Detect Magic is only mentioned, as a way to discern the tree's aura.
Tree Form costs 1 charge and is not a roll, save or spell, so charges is untyped.
Each of Lightning, Thunder, Thunder and Lightning, Lightning Strike and Thunderclap can't be used again until the next dawn once used.
Lightning: when you hit with a melee attack using the staff, you can cause the target to take the extra 2d6 Lightning damage (no action required).
Thunder: when you hit with a melee attack, the target makes the save or has the Stunned condition until the end of your next turn.
Thunder and Lightning: right after a melee hit, as a Bonus Action you use Lightning and Thunder together without expending their daily uses.
Lightning Strike: a 5-foot-wide, 120-foot-long Line as a Magic action. 9d6 on a failed save, half on a success.
Thunderclap: as a Magic action. On a failed save a creature takes 2d6 Thunder damage and has the Deafened condition for 1 minute. On a success it takes half damage only.
It is wielded as a magic Quarterstaff with no stated bonus, dealing normal Quarterstaff damage.
On a hit, you can expend 1 charge to deal the extra 2d10 Necrotic damage.
The save is forced by the same charge as the extra damage. On a failed save the target has Disadvantage for 1 hour on ability checks and saving throws that use Strength or Constitution.
The one charge brings about the 2d10 and the save, so both carry charges 1 and the same label, and the cost is paid once.
While touching it to the ground, as a Magic action you summon an Earth Elemental within 30 feet that obeys you and acts right after you.
It disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, or when you dismiss it as a Bonus Action. The stone can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

damage.appliesWhen: When you hit an Undead with it

notes: The blade exists only after a Bonus Action. It functions as a Longsword with the Finesse property. Proficiency with Longswords or Shortswords gives proficiency with it.
It deals Radiant damage instead of Slashing damage.
It emits sunlight: Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for 15 more feet, adjustable by 5 feet each as a Magic action, between 10 and 30 feet each.

damage.appliesWhen: When you attack a creature with this magic weapon and roll a 20 on the d20 for the attack roll, that target takes an extra 15 Necrotic damage if it isn’t a Construct or an Undead

notes: The roll needs both the 20 and a target that isn't a Construct or an Undead. No shorter single span holds both, so the span is the whole clause.
You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage taken.

damage.appliesWhen: When you attack a creature with this weapon and roll a 20 on the d20 for the attack roll

notes: When you hit an object, maximize your weapon damage dice against it. No typed field holds that.
On the roll of 20 against a creature, the target also gains 1 Exhaustion level.
The extra damage and the save both follow every hit on a creature. On a failed save the target can't regain Hit Points for 1 hour.
The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

damage.appliesWhen: A Fiend or an Undead that touches the talisman

notes: The 8d6 Radiant damage is taken again each time the Fiend or Undead ends its turn holding or carrying the talisman. Item damage has no timing field, so damage is untyped.
Holy Symbol: it can be used as a Holy Symbol. The spell attack bonus applies while you wear or hold it.
Pure Rebuke: a creature you can see on the ground within 120 feet makes the save. A Fiend or Undead has Disadvantage. On a failure it falls into the fissure and is destroyed.
No regaining of charges is stated. When the last charge is expended, the talisman is destroyed, which the charges object cannot hold.
The 1 charge brings about the save and the 4d6, so both carry charges 1 and the same label, and the cost is paid once.
Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to control a Sphere of Annihilation.
When you start your turn in control of a Sphere, as a Magic action you move it 10 feet plus 10 times your Intelligence modifier in feet, not necessarily in a straight line.

damage.appliesWhen: A creature that isn’t a Fiend or an Undead that touches the talisman

notes: The 8d6 Necrotic damage is taken again each time the creature ends its turn holding or carrying the talisman. Item damage has no timing field, so damage is untyped.
Holy Symbol: it can be used as a Holy Symbol. The spell attack bonus applies while you wear or hold it.
Ultimate End: a creature you can see on the ground within 120 feet makes the save. A Celestial has Disadvantage. On a failure it falls into the fissure and is destroyed.
No regaining of charges is stated. When the last charge is expended, the talisman is destroyed, which the charges object cannot hold.
The 1 charge brings about the save and the 4d6, so both carry charges 1 and the same label, and the cost is paid once.

damage.label: Earthquake
damage.appliesWhen: Structures in contact with the ground in that area

notes: While attuned, your Strength is 20 unless it is already 20 or higher.
Clap of Thunder: a 30-foot Cone. Each creature in it makes the Strength save or has the Prone condition.

Earthquake: a 50-foot-radius circle. A creature on the ground that fails the Dexterity save has the Prone condition. A concentrating creature makes the Constitution save or loses Concentration. The fissure is optional: a creature on its spot falls in on a failed save.
The uses entry is Earthquake's.

One use of Earthquake brings about its 50 damage and its three saves, so all carry the label Earthquake. The concentrating save and the fissure save carry the words that tell them apart as appliesWhen.

notes: No attack or damage bonus is stated for the weapon.
A tube holds 1d6 + 1 ounces when found. As a Utilize action you pour 1 or more ounces on a surface within reach. Each ounce dissolves up to 1 square foot of adhesive, including Sovereign Glue.
The extra 2d6 is of the same type as the weapon's normal damage.
The weapon ignores Resistance to Slashing damage.
When you roll a 20 on the attack roll against a creature with at least one head, you cut off a head. The creature dies if it can't survive without it.

The extra 30 Slashing damage falls only on that roll of 20, and only on a creature immune to the beheading or one that spends Legendary Resistance. The 20 and the immunity are in different sentences and no single span holds them, so the roll is left out.

the wand crumbles into dust and is destroyed

notes: As a Magic action expending 1 charge, you choose a point within 120 feet, and the effect is rolled on the 1d100 Wand of Wonder Effects table.
Spells cast from the wand have a save DC of 15, and a spell's range under 120 feet becomes 120 feet.

The spells named in the table (Darkness, Faerie Fire, Fireball, Slow, Stinking Cloud, Gust of Wind, Lightning Bolt, Invisibility, Polymorph, and Enlarge/Reduce as an effect) belong to its rows and are left out of spells and spellEffects. Greater Restoration is only mentioned.
The table rows' own saves (DC 15 Constitution), damage (1d6 Psychic to you, 1 Bludgeoning per gem) and conditions belong to the rows and are not typed on the item.
The DC 15 for spells cast from the wand applies to the table rows' spells. The wand forces no save of its own outside the rows.

The 1 charge pays for a roll on the table, not for a typed roll, save or spell, so charges is untyped. The wand sets the save DC and raises a short range to 120 feet for every spell cast from it, changes no field holds, so spells is untyped.
While the weapon is within your reach and you are attuned, you and allies within 30 feet gain these benefits.
Alarm: each subject sleeping naturally wakes when combat begins, but not from magically induced sleep.
Supernatural Readiness: each subject has Advantage on its Initiative rolls.

As a Magic action you unfold it on a solid surface to form a two-way, 6-foot-diameter portal to a world or plane the GM decides. It stays open until a creature within 5 feet folds it as a Magic action.
After opening a portal, it can't do so again for 1d8 hours.
Each later use before the next dawn has a cumulative 20 percent chance of failing. If it fails, the fan tears into useless, nonmagical tatters.
As a Magic action expending 1 charge, you gain a Fly Speed of 30 feet for 1 hour. If you are flying when it expires, you descend 30 feet per round until you land.
The Fly Speed costs 1 charge and is not a roll, save or spell, so charges is untyped.
As a Magic action the cloak becomes wings that give a Fly Speed of 60 feet for 1 hour or until you end them as a Magic action.
If you are aloft when the wings disappear, you fall. After they disappear, you can't use them again for 1d12 hours.
